title: Scoping to Deployed Agent
subtitle: Take a customer from a scoping document to a governed agent deployment in two weeks, where every stage advances only on evidence signed by the right owner.
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Intake and clarifying questions
practice_prompts.hint: What must intake refuse, and which answers change the design?

practice_prompts.label: Stages, gates and signers
practice_prompts.hint: Name each gate, its signer, its evidence and the deny rules.

practice_prompts.label: The delivered agent and rollout
practice_prompts.hint: Trace one ticket and explain shadow, limited production and rollback.

practice_prompts.label: Limits, cost and stalls
practice_prompts.hint: Which numbers are scripted, what is unbuilt, and how does a no-go look?

rubric: Refuses at intake without a measurable metric, a named SME and named sources, and creates no clock.
Names all seven stages with their days and the signer of each of the six gates.
States the three deny rules and why seniority is not an override.
Distinguishes golden_set_signed_off from eval_baseline_met and security review from data access.
Explains the reuse rate as reused pulls over total pulls (83% for Northwind).
Keeps the LLM out of release decisions and humans in control of sending until autonomy is earned.
Separates the day-14 acceptance rule from the week-4 target and its named owner.
Says the Northwind numbers are scripted and names the unbuilt pieces before being asked.

editorial_review.evidence: Read all 48 captured sections (Interview Guide, Deep Dive, Cheat Sheet and the three-part Full Design) and wrote the casebook from scratch. The opening keeps a term list because SME, FDA, gate, golden set, shadow mode and accelerator library are all used before they could be explained inline, and follows one engagement and one Northwind ticket. The interview guide and Full Design overlapped heavily (gates, days, requirements, limits); each overlap was merged into one walkthrough step while keeping both source tables where they differ (e.g. stage/day/signer vs gate/blocks/signer). Every source table (24 of 25; the old navigation table is consolidated), all three code blocks and all seven figure pairs are retained beside prose that reads them. Added material (blank-page prompt, five follow-up drills, the 3/11 override arithmetic and 5/6 reuse arithmetic) is labelled or derived only from source facts. Reference URLs are the source's own. Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): the captured glossary expanded FDA as Food and Drug Administration → Forward Deployed Architect everywhere, with the term-list note about the mis-expansion removed; the minute-55 summary said two of four mitigations are built → three of four ('which one isn't'), matching the risk table and the code (check_escalation_triggers and the two intake refusals built, scope-change control not), with the visible correction paragraph replaced by a plain statement of the three. November 20 complete maintained-baseline review: Complete maintained casebook: brief, nine walkthrough steps with all tables, figures and pseudocode, all seven deep dives including references and provenance tables, every practice self-check and follow-up answer, the sixty-minute plan, pilot-spend card, level calibration and Quick review.
